{{nihongo|'''Izanagi Shrine'''|伊射奈岐神社 (吹田市山田東)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Settsu Province]].

'''Izanagi Shrine'' (Izanagi Shrine) is located in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}{{ill|Suita|Q653510|qid=Q653510}} Yamada Higashi.

In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, there are two ``Isanagi Shrines'' in the {{ill|Shimashimo district|Q10976940|qid=Q10976940}} section, and one of them is Engi {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikiuchi Shrine}}. The other troupe is said to be {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Saidera, Suita)|Q11379322|qid=Q11379322|lt=a shrine of the same name}}, which is located in Sai-dera Temple and enshrines {{ill|Izanagi|Q813858|qid=Q813858|lt=Isanagi-no-Mikoto}}. The old {{ill|Shakaku|ja|社格|ko|사격 (신토)|zh|社格|qid=Q10444029}} is {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.{{ill|Ban Nobutomo|Q4346747|qid=Q4346747}} Originally only {{ill|Izanami|Q682306|qid=Q682306|lt=Isanami}} was enshrined here, but {{jalink|Jōkan} (Japan)|Q1075635|Jōgan}} to {{ill|Engi (era)|Q1374325|qid=Q1374325}}, it has been proven that the Isanagi god was {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=solicited}} to our company.

=== History ===
According to the shrine's biography, in the year 23 of {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|Q357235|qid=Q357235}}, she was the {{ill|Saikū|Q150845|qid=Q150845}} of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|qid=Q687168}}. |Q11581017}}・{{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Q4388732|qid=Q4388732}}'s instruction led Okamoto Toyotahiko to search for a place to enshrine the five {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Imperial Gods}}, and it is said that he enshrined them in the nearby Ogawa Valley. At first it was called Himemiya Shrine. In {{ill|Ninju|Q1373077|qid=Q1373077}}2 ({{ill|852|Q30383|qid=Q30383}}), Himemiya was moved to Mt. Takaniwa.

{{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jogan}} between the first year ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}) and the fifteenth year of Jogan ({{ill|873|Q30369|qid=Q30369}}) {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Saidera, Suita)|Q11379322|qid=Q11379322|lt=Saidera Shrine}} {{ill|Izanami|Q682306|qid=Q682306|lt=Izanami God}} {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Solicit}}. In 873, the company name was changed from Himemiya to ``Goshagu''. {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}<ref>``Settsushi''</ref><ref>``Settsu Famous Places Zue''</ref> was commonly called Gosha.The main shrine and worship hall were built in {{ill|Kan'ei|Q1192913|qid=Q1192913}}13 ({{ill|1636|Q6885|qid=Q6885}}). In {{ill|1870|Q7741|qid=Q7741}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}3), the current company name was adopted as the official name <ref>``Osakafu Zenshi''</ref>.
{{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}} (Meiji 6), becomes {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. {{ill|1911|Q2076|qid=Q2076}} (Meiji 44), Tsuchiyama Shrine and Tenma Shrine in Yamada no Kami, Daimyo Musa Shrine, and Tenma Shrine in Yamada Shita were merged and relocated to the precincts.

Among the descendants of the first Shinto priest, Toyotahiko Okamoto, is {{ill|Eitarō Okamoto|Q27920598|qid=Q27920598}} ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Vice Minister of Agriculture and Commerce}}, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Norinchukin Bank|Norinchukin Bank|Q2007236|Industrial Union Central Bank}})<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|title=Eitaro Okamoto (8th edition) - "Personnel Koshinroku" database |url=https://jahis.law.nagoya-u.ac.jp/who/docs/who8-5202 |website=jahis.law.nagoya-u.ac.jp |access-date=2022-08-10}}</ref>. Served as the Japanese government representative in {{ill|Geneva|Q71|qid=Q71|lt=Geneva}}.

=== Historical evidence ===
{{Original research|section=1|date=April 2020}} 
* There are two Isanagi Shrines in Suita City ({{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Saidera, Suita)|Q11379322|qid=Q11379322|lt=Saidera Shrine}} and Yamada Higashi Shrine), both of which were founded in {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|Q357235|qid=Q357235}} in the year 23. The Saidera Shrine's shrine biography states, ``From {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōkan}} to {{ill|Engi (era)|Q1374325|qid=Q1374325}} ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}} - In {{ill|922|Q24219|qid=Q24219}}), {{ill|Izanami|Q682306|qid=Q682306|lt=Izana Mikami}} was relocated to the Tohoku region. This was called Himemiya, and the head office was called Okumiya.'' On the other hand, the biography of Yamada Tosha says, ``In the 23rd year of Emperor Yuryaku, Himemiya was founded in Ogawa Valley. Later, Himemiya was relocated to Mt. Takaniwa, and the company name was changed to Goshagu in the 15th year of the Jokan era.''* It is said that both Saidera Shrine and Yamada Higashi Shrine were awarded {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} in the first year of Jogan (859). It is written in ``Records|Q1052981}} that ``he bestowed the rank of Junior Fifth Rank on the god Ishanagi,'' and the place that actually bestowed the divine rank was the {{ill|Izanagi Shrine (Saidera, Suita)|Q11379322|qid=Q11379322|lt=Sai-dera Shrine}} only, but not at Yamada Higashi Shrine. The Edo period Japanese scholar {{ill|Ban Nobutomo|Q4346747|qid=Q4346747}} said, ``Both Isanagi-jin and Izana-mi-jin are the ancestors of the emperor, and since Yamada Higashi-sha did not have the gift that should have been bestowed on the two shrines, Iyanagi-jinja Shrine at Yamada Higashi-sha was solicited from Saidera Shrine during the Jogan to Engi years (859 - 922).''
* However, the Osaka Prefecture Zenshi states that ``Himenomiya was relocated to Mt. Takaniwa in {{ill|Ninju|Q1373077|qid=Q1373077}} 2nd year (852) before Jogan,'' which suggests that Himemiya existed before Kansho.

Arranged in chronological order, the company history of Yamada Higashisha is as follows: ``In the 23rd year of Emperor Yuryaku, the Himemiya was founded in Ogawadani → In the 2nd year of Jinju (852), the Himemiya was relocated to Mt. Takaba → Between the 1st year of the Jogan era and the 15th year of the Jogan era (859 - 873), the shrine of Izanami was solicited from Saidera Shrine → In the 15th year of the Jogan era, the company name was changed to Goshagu Shrine.'' Since the same deity as the enshrined deity is not prayed for, it is thought that the main deity was replaced as a result of the solicitation.

It is currently unknown who the main deity that was originally enshrined at Himemiya was, or even the location of the Ogawa Valley where Himemiya was said to have existed, but its name remains in ``Yamada Ogawa Park'' located southeast of Yamada Higashisha, and a stream still flows next to the park.Near the Kashikiriyama intersection in the former downstream area, there are Okamiki Bridge and Shimookamiki Bridge (currently Yamada Bridge), which are adjacent to {{ill|Daishinboku Shrine|Q85878927|qid=Q85878927}}.
[[File:Okamigi Shrine Takafuda.jpg|Alternative sentence=Okamigi Shrine Takafuda|Thumbnail|Okamigi Shrine_Takafuda]]
The history of Ogamigi Shrine describes how Ogamigi Shrine was founded in the 23rd year of Emperor Yuryaku in response to an oracle from {{ill|Amaterasu|abstract|Q455602|ar|أماتيراسو|ary|أماطيراسو|az|Amaterasu|bcl|Amaterasu|be|Аматэрасу|be_x_old|Аматэрасу|bew|Amatérasu|bg|Аматерасу|ca|Amaterasu|cs|Amaterasu|da|Amaterasu|de|Amaterasu|el|Αματεράσου|eo|Amaterasu|es|Amaterasu|et|Amaterasu|eu|Amaterasu|fa|آماتراسو|fi|Amaterasu|fr|Amaterasu|gl|Amaterasu|he|אמטראסו|hi|अमातेरसु|hr|Amaterasu|hu|Amateraszu Ómikami|hy|Ամատերասու Օմիկամի|id|Amaterasu|it|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|jv|Amaterasu|ka|ამატერასუ|ko|아마테라스 오미카미|la|Amaterasu|lb|Amaterasu|lt|Amaterasu|lv|Amaterasu|min|Amaterasu|ml|അമതേരസു|mni|ꯑꯃꯇꯦꯔꯁꯨ ꯑꯣꯃꯤꯀꯃꯤ|ms|Amaterasu|nl|Amaterasu|nn|Amaterasu|no|Amaterasu|or|ଆମାତେରାଶୁ|pa|ਆਮਾਤੇਰਸ|pl|Amaterasu|pt|Amaterasu|ro|Amaterasu|ru|Аматэрасу|sco|Amaterasu|sh|Amaterasu|simple|Amaterasu Ōmikami|sk|Amaterasu Ómikami|sl|Amaterasu|sr|Аматерасу|su|Amaterasu|sv|Amaterasu|ta|அமதெரசு|th|อามาเตราซุ|tl|Amaterasu|tok|jan sewi suli Amatelasu|tr|Amaterasu|uk|Аматерасу|uz|Amaterasu|vi|Amaterasu|wuu|天照大神|zh|天照大神|zh_min_nan|Amaterasu|zh_yue|天照大神|qid=Q455602}}. It is said that while en route to the shrine of Toyouke no Okami}} from {{ill|Tanba Province|cs|Tanba (provincie)|de|Provinz Tamba|es|Provincia de Tanba|fa|ولایت تانبا|fr|Province de Tanba|gl|Provincia de Tanba|id|Provinsi Tamba|it|Tanba (provincia)|ja|丹波国|ko|단바국|lt|Tambos žemė|nl|Tamba (provincie)|pt|Província de Tanba|ru|Тамба (провинция)|simple|Tamba Province|sk|Tanba (provincia)|sr|Провинција Тамба|tr|Tamba (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Тамба|zh|丹波國|zh_min_nan|Tanba-kok|qid=Q954511}} to {{ill|Ise Province|be|Ісэ (правінцыя)|ckb|پارێزگای ئیسێ|cs|Provincie Ise|de|Provinz Ise|es|Provincia de Ise|eu|Ise probintzia|fa|ولایت ایسه|fi|Isen provinssi|fr|Province d'Ise|gl|Provincia de Ise|hak|Yî-sṳ-koet|id|Provinsi Ise|it|Ise (provincia)|ja|伊勢国|ko|이세국|lt|Isės žemė|nl|Ise (provincie)|pt|Província de Ise|ru|Исэ (провинция)|simple|Ise Province|sk|Ise (provincia)|sr|Провинција Исе|tr|Ise (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ісе|zh|伊勢國|zh_min_nan|Ise-kok|zh_yue|伊勢國|qid=Q864166}}, a temporary shrine was built on the local sacred tree and remained there for over a year.
:'''In the course of the Sengu, {{ill|Settsu Province|Q864163|qid=Q864163}} He built a shrine in Mishima-go Okamigi and lived there for over a year, and now he is the only Okamikigami...'''
Since Okamiki-jinja Shrine, which appears in the shrine legend, was founded in the 23rd year of Emperor Yuryaku, just like Himemiya, it is likely that the temporary shrine site was once again used for rituals and became Himemiya.

The Yamada Higashi-sha biography says, ``Princess Saigu Princess of Ise Jingu, Wahime (*Princess daughter of Emperor Yuryaku) Based on the teachings of {{ill|Princess Wakatarashihime|Q55533316|qid=Q55533316|lt=Princess Kushimatahime}} [also known as Princess Chikatarihime]'s teachings, Toyashihiko Okamoto (Osada no Mikoto) established a sacred place in this land where the five gods should be enshrined.Due to this, the name was changed from {{ill|Yamada|Q11470062|qid=Q11470062|lt=Ise Yamada}} and became ``{{ill|Yamadagahara|Q11470061|qid=Q11470061|lt=Yamadagahara}}.'' However, the history of this biography is somewhat skeptical due to the following points.

# There is nothing in chronicles or myths that connects Ise's {{ill|Yamada|Q11470062|qid=Q11470062|lt=Yamadagahara}} with Isanagi and Izanami.
# Ebisu no Kami is enshrined at Goshagu Shrine, but Ebisu worship is a later deity that began with the construction of Nishinomiya Ebisu Shrine at the end of the Heian period.
# Gosha Shrine's {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|Q2564508|qid=Q2564508|lt=Amagoyane Mikoto}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshikumone|Q91088537|qid=Q91088537|lt=Amanin Kumane Mikoto}} are {{ill|Ujigami|Q767655|qid=Q767655}} of {{ill|Fujiwara clan|ar|فوجيوارا (عشيرة)|be|Фудзівара (род)|br|Klann Fujiwara|ca|Clan Fujiwara|cs|Fudžiwara|de|Fujiwara (Familie)|el|Αδελφότητα Φούτζιγουαρα|es|Clan Fujiwara|eu|Fujiwara klana|fa|خاندان فوجیوارا|fi|Fujiwara-klaani|fr|Clan Fujiwara|he|בית פוג'יווארה|hr|Fujiwara (klan)|hu|Fudzsivara család|id|Klan Fujiwara|it|Clan Fujiwara|ja|藤原氏|ko|후지와라씨|la|Domus Fujiwara|ms|Suku Fujiwara|nl|Fujiwara (familie)|pl|Fujiwara (ród)|pt|Clã Fujiwara|ru|Фудзивара (род)|sh|Fujiwara (klan)|sk|Fudžiwara|sr|Фуџивара клан|sv|Fujiwara|ta|புஜிவாரா குலம்|th|ตระกูลฟูจิวาระ|tr|Fujiwara boyu|uk|Рід Фудзівара|vi|Gia tộc Fujiwara|zh|藤原氏|zh_classical|藤原氏|zh_min_nan|Fujiwara--sī|qid=Q641628}}.
# In ancient times, powerful families did not worship the guardian deities of other powerful families, even if they were members of the imperial family.
# In the era of Emperor Yuryaku, the {{ill|Katsuragi clan|Q11620908|qid=Q11620908}}, {{ill|Ōtomo clan (ancient)|Q17227938|qid=Q17227938}}, and {{ill|Kose clan|Q11479778|qid=Q11479778}} were on the rise, and it would have been impossible to enshrine the guardian deity of the Fujiwara clan (Nakatomi clan), which was a small and powerful clan at the time, apart from these powerful clans.During the Jogan period, when Kansho was held, Inari worship, which enshrined Uka no Mitama no Kami, was very popular. Inari worship began in the Wado era (708-715) with the founding of Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine by the Hata clan, and reached its peak during the Jogan period, when Emperor Junna granted him the rank of ``Junior Fifth Rank Lower'' in the 4th year of Tencho (827), and the highest rank of ``Shoichii'' in 5th year of Tenkei (942). Inari Daimyojin (Uka no Mitamajin) is enshrined in the set shrine of Yamada Higashisha, and it is thought that this Inari Daimyojin, not Ebisu no Kami, was originally enshrined as one of the five shrines. However, even if the Ebisu no kami of Goshagu Shrine was Uka no Mitama no Kami, it would be unreasonable to assume that Goshagu Shrine was worshiped in Ise during the era of Emperor Yuryaku. Goshagu is a Goshagu shrine when all five pillars are present, and it cannot be called a Goshagu shrine if one pillar is missing. For this reason, it is doubtful and unreliable that the other four pillars were also enshrined in Ise. It is likely that the shrine biography was altered by the Fujiwara clan after the solicitation, and the original shrine biography is ``{{ill|Saikū|Q150845|qid=Q150845}} Princess of Ise Grand Shrine, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Princess Chisashihime}}, Okamoto Toyashihiko (Osada no Mikoto) established this sacred place to enshrine {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Toyouke Okami}}. (Ise City)|Q11470062|Ise Yamada}} and changed its name to {{ill|Yamadagahara|Q11470061|qid=Q11470061|lt=Yamadagahara}}.

The deity enshrined in Ise Yamada in Ise is Toyouke no Okami, not Izana Mikami.The name of the place {{ill|Yamada|Q11470062|qid=Q11470062|lt=Ise Yamadagahara}} was moved because the main deity of Himemiya (Karigu) was Toyouke Okami, which is {{ill|Sengū|Q2271023|qid=Q2271023}}; conversely, it is because the place name of Yamadagahara was moved that proves that the main deity of Himemiya is Toyouke Okami.

Furthermore, ``Ogawadani,'' where the temporary shrine was located, is thought to be the current ``Shakudani.'' Shaku is a unit of length and is not related to tani.

This is probably because ``Karimiya no Tani'' was mistakenly written as ``Kuramiya no Tani,'' and the abbreviation ``Kurutani'' was later rewritten as ``Shakutani.''

* Main shrine (Tangible Cultural Property designated by Osaka Prefecture) - Rebuilt in {{ill|Kan'ei|Q1192913|qid=Q1192913}}13 ({{ill|1636|Q6885|qid=Q6885}}). The Gokensha {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684}} cypress bark roof is rare in Osaka Prefecture.

=== Access ===
